what_it_does: sums per-document term counts from process_doc into one dict and counts, for each term, how many documents contain it

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: each per-doc `counts` dict has unique keys, so `terms[term]['docs'] += 1` inside the first loop gives the same document frequency; the second pass of T terms x D dicts (T*D hash probes plus a throwaway list per term) disappears

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: `total_count` is never read; deleting it removes one list and one sum per document

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: the list inside `sum` is part of the per-term scan; removing the scan (label a) removes it too

what_it_does: counts every n-gram window (1..term_length) of a token list that contains no common word

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: the membership `w in common_words` of a word does not change between windows; precomputing one boolean per token and slicing it removes the lambda call per word per window and leaves one C-level `any` over a slice of bools

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: `doc[i:i+win_len]` is sliced twice for every kept window; binding it once saves one slice allocation per window

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: with the default empty `common_words` the any(map(lambda)) can never be true; a guard skips it entirely, removing a map object, a lambda frame per word and the any() call per window

decisions.label: d
decisions.why: `map(lambda ...)` pays a Python frame per word; card C10.S2 repair 3 measured comprehension over map+lambda as cheaper

what_it_does: returns the summed counts of title and content n-grams for one document

decisions.label: a

what_it_does: collects the set of all title/content tokens of documents that have both fields

what_it_does: writes the accepted terms, one per line, to a fixed path

what_it_does: reads a stop-word file into a set
